Thought: To determine the correct ordering of compounds from most to least reactive in an electrophilic aromatic substitution, I need to consider the effects of substituents on the reactivity of the aromatic ring. The electron-donating and electron-withdrawing properties of the substituents will influence the reactivity.

1. OC1=CC=CC=C1 (anisole) has an -OCH3 group, which is an electron-donating group through resonance, making the aromatic ring more reactive toward electrophilic aromatic substitution. It is expected to be the most reactive.

2. CC1=CC=CC=C1 (toluene) has a -CH3 group, which is also an electron-donating group but less effective than -OCH3. The aromatic ring is more reactive than benzene but less reactive than that with an -OCH3 group.

3. ClC1=CC=CC=C1 (chlorobenzene) has a -Cl group, which is an electron-withdrawing group through inductive effects, although it can donate electrons by resonance. It generally deactivates the aromatic ring compared to benzene, so it is expected to be the least reactive.

Based on these considerations, the order from most to least reactive is: OC1=CC=CC=C1, CC1=CC=CC=C1, ClC1=CC=CC=C1.
